name: Apollo 11
note: Landed in Mare Tranquillitatis with the Sun 10.7° up in the east and Earth 59° up in the west.

name: Apollo 12
note: Landed in Oceanus Procellarum near Surveyor 3 with the Sun only 5.2° above the horizon.

name: Apollo 14
note: Landed at Fra Mauro with the Sun 10.4° up and Earth 66° up.

name: Apollo 15
note: Landed at Hadley-Apennine with the Sun 12.1° up; first mission with the Lunar Roving Vehicle.

name: Apollo 16
note: Landed in the Descartes highlands with the Sun 14.8° up and Earth 77° up.

name: Apollo 17
note: Landed at Taurus-Littrow with the Sun 13.3° up and Earth 46° up.

name: Luna 9
note: First soft landing on the Moon, in Oceanus Procellarum.

name: Surveyor 1
note: First US soft landing, in Oceanus Procellarum.

name: Surveyor 3
note: Landed in a crater that Apollo 12 later reached on foot; the crew brought parts of it home.

name: Chang'e 3
note: Landed in northern Mare Imbrium and deployed the Yutu rover.

name: Chang'e 4
note: First far-side landing, in Von Kármán crater; Earth never rises, so all contact goes via the Queqiao relay.

name: Chang'e 5
note: Sample return from northern Oceanus Procellarum near Mons Rümker.

name: Chang'e 6
note: First far-side sample return, from the southern Apollo basin; contact only via the Queqiao-2 relay.

name: Chandrayaan-3 (Statio Shiv Shakti)
note: Landed at local sunrise; Pragyan and Vikram were put to sleep on 2 and 4 Sep 2023 and did not wake after the night.

name: SLIM
note: Landed nose-down with west-facing solar cells, so it had power only once the Sun moved west.

name: IM-1 Odysseus
note: Landed tipped over near Malapert A, about 1.5 km from target; last contact 29 Feb 2024.

name: IM-2 Athena
note: Landed on its side in a 20 m crater on Mons Mouton; its panels could not recharge and it ended on 7 Mar 2025.

name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
note: Landed upright in Mare Crisium; filmed Earth eclipsing the Sun on 14 Mar 2025 and ran a few hours past sunset.

name: Vikram (Chandrayaan-2)
note: Failed landing: crashed during descent; this is the impact site found in LRO images.

name: Beresheet
note: Failed landing: crashed in Mare Serenitatis during descent.

name: HAKUTO-R Mission 1
note: Failed landing: contact was lost moments before touchdown near Atlas crater; debris seen by LRO.

name: Luna 25
note: Failed landing: struck the rim of Pontecoulant G, about 400 km short of its 69.5°S target.

name: HAKUTO-R Mission 2 Resilience
note: Failed landing: hard landing in Mare Frigoris; LRO saw a dark smudge at the impact point.

name: Blue Moon MK1
note: Approximate: centre of the Shackleton connecting ridge region, its named target; not yet launched.

name: Chang'e 7
note: Reported preferred site, a sunlit peak next to Shackleton crater; no final site published, launch slipped from Aug 2026.

name: Griffin Mission 1
note: Approximate: centre of Nobile crater, the named target region; carries the FLIP rover.

name: IM-3
note: Approximate: centre of the Reiner Gamma swirl, its named target; carries Lunar Vertex and CADRE.

name: Blue Ghost Mission 2
note: Approximate: centre of Nassau crater on the far side, its named target; no direct line of sight to Earth.

name: CP-12 Schrödinger basin
note: Approximate: centre of Schrödinger basin, the CLPS CP-12 target on the far side near the south pole.

name: Haworth (Artemis III region)
note: Approximate centre of the region polygon (2022 outline); one of nine Artemis III candidate regions, Oct 2024.

name: Malapert Massif (Artemis III region)
note: Approximate centre of the region polygon (2022 outline); one of nine Artemis III candidate regions, Oct 2024.

name: Mons Mouton Plateau (Artemis III region)
note: Approximate centre (LROC NAC mosaic of the region); one of nine Artemis III candidate regions, Oct 2024.

name: Mons Mouton (Artemis III region)
note: Approximate centre of the 2022 Leibnitz Beta Plateau polygon, renamed Mons Mouton; Artemis III region, Oct 2024.

name: Nobile Rim 1 (Artemis III region)
note: Approximate centre of the region polygon (2022 outline); one of nine Artemis III candidate regions, Oct 2024.

name: Nobile Rim 2 (Artemis III region)
note: Approximate centre of the region polygon (2022 outline); one of nine Artemis III candidate regions, Oct 2024.

name: de Gerlache Rim 2 (Artemis III region)
note: Approximate centre of the region polygon (2022 outline); one of nine Artemis III candidate regions, Oct 2024.

name: Shackleton connecting ridge
note: Most illuminated point in the LOLA maps: lit 89.0% of the time at the surface, 93.1% at 10 m (site 1).

name: Connecting ridge, region 1
note: Centre of region 1 of Barker et al. 2021 (5 m map): over 70% average sunlight at 1 m in 2024 and 2025.

name: Connecting ridge, region 4
note: Centre of region 4 of Barker et al. 2021 (5 m map): over 70% average sunlight at 1 m in 2024 and 2025.

name: Connecting ridge, region 6
note: Centre of region 6 of Barker et al. 2021 (5 m map): over 70% average sunlight at 1 m in 2024 and 2025.

name: Shackleton rim
note: LOLA high-illumination point on the Shackleton rim near the pole, lit 86.7% of the time at the surface (site 4).

name: Peak near Shackleton
note: LOLA high-illumination point on the ridge east of Shackleton, lit 85.5% of the time at the surface (site 7).

name: de Gerlache rim
note: LOLA high-illumination point on the de Gerlache rim, lit 84.6% of the time at the surface (site 11).

name: Malapert peak
note: LOLA high-illumination point on Mons Malapert, lit 81.8% of the time at the surface (site 23).

name: Bussey et al. 2010 point
note: Most illuminated point (86% of the year) in a Kaguya-topography model, near the Shackleton rim.
